title: Carver / qoppac: simple breakout trading rule (range-position forecast, pysystemtrade)
why: Continuous rule, not a channel entry: for each lookback N in 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320 business days, roll_max and roll_min over N closes; roll_mean = (roll_max + roll_min)/2; raw = 40 x (price - roll_mean) / (roll_max - roll_min), so about -20 to +20; smooth with an EWMA of span max(int(N/4),1) (the post's example: 63 on 250); the average of the six forecasts is the signal (the post's own cap is +/-20, its scalars are 0.71-0.84 per variant, pooled). Position = forecast / 10 (average absolute forecast about 10), one unit per instrument, daily rebalance, sign-to-size. Sits outside the engine's rule set (no continuous forecast), so the builder writes it as a daily script on closes up to yesterday, with half-round-trip cost per unit of change and 0.5 bp swap per day. Markets: XAUUSD, XAGUSD, WTIUSD, SPXUSD, USDJPY, EURUSD, AUDCAD (daily closes from marketdata). Note: the post has no Sharpe or cost figures; the 10-day variant is costly (turnover about 89 trades a year), so test 20-320 first. Suits Funded (low turnover, daily) more than Hydra. Not the rejected 'channel breakout' entry rule: that was a binary Donchian entry; this is a smoothed range-position forecast.
result: Gate halves FAIL: net Sharpe 0.14 (0.09 to 2017 / 0.18 from 2018), 0.01 at 1.5x cost; research/carver_range_breakout.py

title: Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling & Schrimpf (2017), Currency Value, Review of Financial Studies 30(2), read in full (54 pages)
why: Rule (Sec. 3.4.1, eq. 7-8): signal = 5-year change in the log real exchange rate, q = p - p* - s (s = USD per unit of foreign currency, CPI prices, base 1970Q1; a higher q is a stronger dollar). Each quarter rank the currencies on the signal and go long the cheap ones (low 5-year change in q, i.e. weak RER vs USD) and short the rich ones, equal-weight rank portfolio or linear weights c_t(x_j - mean), dollar-neutral, rebalanced at quarter end, excess return = spot change plus interest differential. Paper result (22 currencies, 1976Q1-2014Q1, gross, no costs stated): raw 5-year RER rank portfolio SR 0.50 (Table 4), quarterly turnover about 18% (footnote 17). Only the raw PPP version is testable: the fundamentals-adjusted version (SR 0.8-0.9, Table 5) needs GDP per capita, export quality (IMF) and net foreign assets, not free to us. Expected weakness, stated up front: the paper's spread is driven by emerging currencies (Turkey, Mexico, Indonesia, Hungary), so on our 7 USD majors (EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, USDCAD, USDCHF, NZDUSD) with about 0.2 of the paper's dispersion the edge may vanish. Quarterly trades, so the cost is trivial. Suits Funded only (a slow, low-turnover diversifier and keep-the-account leg); not Hydra (a quarter-long hold cannot reach 5x in a month). Needs data item data_fred_cpi_g10 first.
result: finder 2026-10-22: blocked on data_fred_cpi_g10 (rejected: no complete free CPI set through 2026); expected weak on the USD majors (the paper's spread comes from emerging currencies). Not tested.

title: Moreira & Muir (2016/2017), Volatility-Managed Portfolios, NBER WP 22208 (read in full, 57 pages incl. appendix)
why: Rule (main text, f^sigma_{t+1} = (c / RV_t^2) * f_{t+1}): RV_t = realized variance of daily returns over the previous month (22 daily returns in a daily version); the managed exposure is c / RV^2 times the buy-and-hold exposure, rebalanced from closes up to yesterday. c sets the managed series' full-sample std equal to buy-and-hold's; for us fit c on data to 2017 only, then freeze it. Cap the scale (test 1x, 2x) since the paper's leverage-cap table in the appendix shows the gain depends on capping. Paper results (monthly, 1926-2015): managed market factor raises Sharpe; OECD 20-country check gives a mean Sharpe change of 0.15 and a positive change in 80% of countries (Fig 8). Markets: SPXUSD and XAUUSD on daily closes (equity-factor paper; the gold leg is an extension and must be labelled so), USDJPY and EURUSD as a check. Costs: half round-trip per unit of position change plus 0.5 bp swap per day. Needs a daily script (the spec engine has no vol-scaling rule). Suits Funded (drawdown control, keep-the-account leg); weak for Hydra (it trims size and does not give the 5x path).
result: FAIL at halves 0.40/0.44, DSR 0.008; vol scaling adds no Sharpe over buy-and-hold in both halves (SPX -0.24/-0.09 at cap 2); research/volmanaged_mm.py

title: Breedon & Ranaldo, Intraday patterns in FX returns and order flow (SNB WP 2011-04 / QMUL WP 694; Dec 2008 draft read in full pp1-14)
why: Gap: EURUSD has no leg (gaps.json). Rule (Table 5, EBS 1997-2007, bid/ask costs): EURUSD short 07:00-13:00 GMT, long 13:00-21:00 GMT, one trade each per weekday; paper net Sharpe 1.3 (short) and 0.9 (long) after spread. Reason: local participants net buy foreign currency in their own hours, so EUR weakens in European hours and strengthens in US hours (order-flow evidence). Paper also shows the other pairs (USDJPY, GBPUSD, USDCHF, AUDUSD) are NOT profitable after costs, so the belief gate rests on the order-flow story plus year-by-year stability (Fig 2), not on a basket. Test on 2010-2025 M1 (to 2025-09-30), same hours in server time with DST handling, skip 21:00-01:00 rollover (exit by 21:00 GMT is before it), real FTMO EURUSD spread. Expected weakness: 2008 draft is old, sample ends 2007, effect may have decayed; do not tune hours (use 07-13 and 13-21 as is; report halves 2010-17 / 2018+). Corr: against the quartet (seasonal session) and fix/cross legs must be checked; EURUSD itself carries 0% risk now. Suits Funded; Hydra only as small add-on. Not the rejected round-number or overnight families.

title: Meta-labeling sizing of the AurumBreakout leg (Lopez de Prado, AFML ch. 3.6; Joubert, Meta-Labeling: Calibration and Position Sizing, J. Financial Data Science)
why: Gap: the book's 19 losing months since 2018 (gaps.json), breakout is the largest weight (0.25). Primary model = the existing breakout leg unchanged (side and exits fixed; take every trade the leg takes on USDJPY, EURJPY, GBPUSD, XAUUSD, EURUSD with the leg's own parameters from research/breakout_markets.py). Meta label = 1 if the trade's net R > 0. Features, all known at entry: ATR(14)/ATR(100) ratio, 20-day realised vol percentile, distance of entry from 20-day mean in ATRs, entry hour, weekday, prior 5-trade hit rate of the same market, prior-day range/ATR, month-end flag. Model: sklearn logistic regression (L2) and a shallow LightGBM (depth 2, 100 trees) as a check; expanding walk-forward, retrain each January on all earlier trades with a 10-day purge, first test year 2012, so both halves (2012-17, 2018+) are out of sample. Use: size = 0.5 + 0.5 x calibrated p, or skip when p < 0.40, never above 1x, so it can only trim the leg. Published basis: meta-labeling is the López de Prado method for sizing a fixed-side primary model (only the Hudson and Thames explainer was readable in full; the book chapter and Joubert paper are paywalled, so belief rests on the method plus the 5-market pooling). Differs from the rejected meta_label_hydra (2026-10-22: 2,896 tester trades of Hydra, no skill, tiny sample): different leg, about 15 years of trades pooled across 5 markets, past-only features, walk-forward from 2012. Closest rejected family in candidates.md is 'daily ML'; this is trade-level sizing, not a daily direction forecast. Pass test: the sized leg's Sharpe >= the plain leg in both halves, lower worst month, corr to book unchanged. If no lift over a random-keep at the same rate (3 seeds), reject, as with Hydra. Suits Funded (drawdown and losing-month control); Hydra no.
result: gate book: 2018+ book 3.34 -> 3.32 replacing breakout (needs +0.03); AUC 0.51-0.53, sized 1.06 vs plain 1.04, random keep 0.87-1.01

title: Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone (2025), The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing (SSRN 5122748), pp1-22 read, pages 23-76 not read (robustness, appendix)
why: Gap: US indices (4% of risk), cross-asset flow style, daily horizon, and the book losing months. Rule: simulate a 60/40 portfolio of S&P 500 and 10y Treasury (eq. in Sec 1.2): w(t+1)=w(1+Rsp)/(w(1+Rsp)+(1-w)(1+R10y)), target 60%. Threshold signal_t = mean over delta=0,0.1,...,2.5% of (w_t - 0.60), where w resets to 0.60 whenever |w-0.60|>delta. Calendar signal_t = w_t - 0.60 with reset on the last business day of each month, used only in the last 5 trading days of the month. Both predict next-day S&P minus 10y return NEGATIVELY (t about 4; Table 1 coefficients -0.42 Threshold, -0.30 Calendar*week4; 1 sd = about 17-20 bp next day; reverts within 2 weeks; effect significant only from early 2000s). Paper: front-running S&P/10y futures long-short on these signals Sharpe > 1, 1997-2023 (gross; page of the Sharpe table not located in the pages read). Our test: equity side only, since FTMO has no bond CFD: short US500.cash next day when signal > 0 and long when < 0 (threshold signal anytime; calendar signal in last-5-day window), one position per day, cost = US500 spread + FTMO swap from docs/ftmo_specs.json. Bond leg input: R10y approx = -8 x change in DGS10 (percent/100) + DGS10/252 from FRED DGS10 daily (free CSV, see data_fred_dgs10); S&P daily close-to-close from marketdata. Same parameters on US100.cash and GER40 if held as the 3-market belief check (paper: signal extends to international equity). Expected weakness: published sample ends 2023-03, flow edge may have decayed; equity-only leg loses the bond half of the spread. Different from rejected noise leg/overnight and the leveraged-ETF rebalancing idea (single stocks): this is pension month-end flow on the index. Suits Funded (daily, low risk); Hydra small add-on.
result: Gate halves 0.19/0.32 (to 2017/2018 on) and book 3.34->3.26; 1.5x Sharpe 0.18; other markets NSX 0.08, GRX -0.20, JPX -0.04. research/rebalancing_signal.py

title: Quantpedia (2026): MA200 trend filter + 2-day pullback, 1-day hold, multi-asset (SPY, EEM, IEF, FXE, GLD, DBC)
why: Gap: days horizon (thin), mean-reversion style on markets other than the dollar pairs, EURUSD (no leg), and the book's losing months (a long-only dip-buy in uptrends should be uncorrelated with the breakout/trend legs). Rule as published (article read in full; its costs are not stated, so costs are ours): long at the close when the close is above its 200-day SMA AND the last 2 daily returns (days t and t-1) are both negative; exit at the close of the next trading day (1-day hold); long only; invested about 21% of days. Article results, daily ETFs 2006-2025: equal-weight portfolio Sharpe 0.95 (annual return 8.96%, max drawdown -25%), single ETFs Sharpe 0.11-0.22 (win rate above 55%), positive Sharpe in all four five-year windows (2011-15 0.69, 2021-25 1.25); 3-down-day version Sharpe 0.78, 7-day hold 0.54, MA150 0.97, MA50 0.85, so the result is smooth, not a single spike. Article has inconsistencies (3 versus 2 down days in the text, sweep size 100 vs 600) and its sweep was chosen on min Sharpe, so use only the stated MA200 / 2 down days / 1-day hold, do not re-sweep. Our test: daily script, signal on closes up to yesterday, return of the next day, cost = half the round-trip spread per side plus the FTMO swap from docs/ftmo_specs.json. Markets, same parameters, belief by 3+ markets: SPXUSD, NSXUSD, XAUUSD, GRXEUR, JPXJPY, EURUSD (also report USDJPY, AUDCAD as a check); also test the equal-weight basket with one unit of risk split across the active signals (as the article does), because single markets are expected near Sharpe 0.2 and the gain comes from the basket. Report halves (to 2017 / 2018 on), 1.5x cost, corr to the book (expect near zero or negative against breakout, hold, noise) and book gain. Differs from the engine's rejected f_reversal_* grid (2026-10-23, all FAIL at halves): those fade the last 1 or 5 day return both ways with no trend filter; this is long-only, conditional on an uptrend and on 2 consecutive down days. Not daily ML, not the VIX filter family. Not expressible as an engine spec (its trend filter is the 20-day return, not MA200). Suits Funded (low exposure, 1-day holds); Hydra no.
result: gates FAIL at halves: basket Sharpe -0.13 / -0.01, 1.5x -0.31; 5/8 markets profitable; research/ma200_pullback.py

why: Gap: weeks+ horizon (thin), gold; a bond-conditioned gold trend should differ from the plain hold leg in 2022-type regimes. Published sample 1969-2025 (GLD, IEF as proxies). Our test: month-end signal, hold next month. title: Option-expiration-week long on index CFDs (Stivers & Sun, S&P 100 stocks; Quantpedia)
why: Gap: US indices (4% of risk), weekly horizon (thin), calendar/flow style, uncorrelated long-only equity exposure on 4 days a month. title: Dao, McGroarty, Urquhart (2016), A calendar effect: weekend overreaction (and subsequent reversal) in spot FX rates, JMulFin 37-38 (read in full, 22 pages)
why: Gap: EURUSD (no leg), weeks/days horizon, mean-reversion style, FX majors outside the quartet/breakout legs; trades about 10% of weeks so it should be near-zero corr with the book. Rule (Sec 3.1-3.2, Tables 4-9): weekend gap = ln(Monday open / Friday close) (paper: Monday open = Sunday 22:00 GMT, Friday close = 22:00 GMT; on FTMO data use first M1 bar of the week and last bar of Friday). Large gap = top or bottom 5% quantile of past weekend gaps of the same pair (5-year window 2002-06, then recursive or rolling; we use a rolling 260-week window, past weeks only). Trade at the Monday open OPPOSITE to the gap (short after top-5% gap, long after bottom-5%), exit at Friday close (one-week horizon, the most significant; 1-day and 3-day horizons are weaker). One position per pair per week. Paper results, 7 majors 2007-2014 out of sample, round-trip cost 0.08% and interest included: abnormal weekly alpha NZDUSD 0.19-0.20% (t>3), GBPUSD 0.07%, CHFUSD 0.05%, EURUSD 0.04% (n.s.), JPY/CAD/AUD about 0; majors group alpha 0.05-0.06% a week (t about 2.5); max drawdown 2-24%; reversal larger after upward gaps (top 5%: EURUSD -0.45% next week, NZDUSD -1.16%) than after downward gaps (bottom 5%: +0.43% panel mean). Panel-mean one-week reversal in Table 4 is -0.33%/+0.43% (top/bottom 5%). Our test: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, AUDCAD with identical parameters (belief by 3+ markets; do not pick pairs by result), real FTMO spread (about 1-2 bp, far below the paper cost 8 bp, so costs are friendlier) plus FTMO swap for the 5 nights from docs/ftmo_specs.json; report halves (2010-17 / 2018 on), 1.5x cost, per-pair Sharpe, trade count, corr to the book and book gain. Expected weakness: sample ends 2014, few trades per pair (about 30 a decade at 5% each side), the effect may have decayed like other published FX calendar effects (Breedon-Ranaldo failed halves); a Sharpe 0.2-0.5 basket is the aim. Differs from the dropped Monday gap fill statistics (intraday vendor fill rates, no net test) and from the rejected round-number and daily reversal grids (this is a weekly hold after a rare gap). Suits Funded; Hydra no.
result: Gate halves FAIL: basket Sharpe 0.02 to 2017 / 0.32 from 2018 (1.5x -0.03 / 0.25); book 2018+ 3.34 -> 3.32. Per pair EURUSD 0.46, NZDUSD 0.38, USDCAD 0.28, rest about 0. research/dao_weekend_gap.py, docs/candidates.json dao_gap

title: Caporale & Plastun (2019), Price Overreactions in the Forex and Trading Strategies, Brunel WP 19-09 (pp1-14 read; remainder is appendix tables)
why: Gap: EURUSD (no leg), days horizon, Asian-session timing, mean-reversion after shocks; trades ~6-8 days a year per pair so near-zero corr with book expected. Rule (Sec 3-4): daily return R=Close/Open-1 (open to close of the day, gaps excluded). Positive overreaction when R > mean_n + k*sd_n, negative when R < mean_n - k*sd_n, k=2; paper does not state n, so use n=20 days of past daily returns fixed, no sweep. Strategy 2 (the one to test first): at the start of the day AFTER an overreaction day open a position opposite to the overreaction and close it at the start of the European session (paper: 07:00-09:00 broker time; use 08:00 fixed, no tuning); paper finds the contrarian move only in Asia, 00:00-09:00. Paper results 2008-2018, hourly MetaQuotes data, NO costs, t-tests vs random: positive overreaction fade EURUSD 0.77%/yr (67 trades, 66% wins), USDJPY 1.37%, AUDUSD 2.29%, EURJPY 2.11%, USDCAD none; negative overreaction fade EURUSD 0.5% (not sig), USDJPY 2.0%, AUDUSD 1.7%, EURJPY 1.8% (n.s.), USDCAD 0.6% n.s. Strategy 1 (optional second leg): enter in the direction of the move when the day open-to-now return first crosses +/-2 sd (past-only sd) and exit at day end; paper reports 83-93% wins, which looks like look-ahead (it uses the day close to classify), so test it only with the real-time trigger and treat as intraday momentum close to the existing noise leg (corr check). Our test: M1 data 2010-2025-09-30, pairs EURUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, EURJPY, USDCAD (same parameters on all, belief by 5 markets), real FTMO spread, rollover 23:00-01:00 excluded (lesson 9: enter at 01:00 server and report; also run the 01:00 entry version), halves 2010-17 / 2018 on, 1.5x cost. Expected weakness: paper has no costs and only ~60 trades a pair in 11 years, effect 0.5-2%/yr so a net Sharpe 0.2-0.4 is the aim; the rollover snap-back may be the whole effect. Differs from rejected dao_gap (weekly, weekend gap) and f_reversal grids (every day, no shock filter, hold to close). Suits Funded; Hydra no.
result: gates FAIL at halves: book Sharpe 0.62 to 2017 / -0.00 from 2018 (1.5x: 0.54 / -0.13); book gain 3.34 -> 3.24; ~270 trades a pair, AUDUSD gross -2.7 bp/trade from 2018. research/overreaction_fx.py

title: Variance risk premium as a timing signal: Bollerslev, Tauchen & Zhou (2009), Expected stock returns and variance risk premia, RFS 22(11); applied to gold, US500 and EURUSD
why: Gap: volatility-premium style (none in book), EURUSD (no leg), weeks horizon. Paper (equities, 1990-2005): VRP = implied variance minus realized variance predicts S&P returns best at 1-3 month horizons, positive sign (high VRP -> higher future returns). Abstract and steer-level definitions only; builder must read the paper in full before testing. Rule to test (steer.md data, no options needed): every Monday compute gap = implied vol minus 22-day realized vol (annualized close-to-close from our daily bars, past-only, IV lagged one day). IV series: GVZCLS for XAUUSD, VIXCLS for US500, EVZCLS for EURUSD (ends 2025-03-11, so EURUSD sample ends then). Signal: gap in its top third of the trailing 252 days -> long the asset for a fixed hold; else flat. Holds 5, 10, 20 trading days as three fixed variants, report all, no pick on one half. Same parameters on all three markets (belief by 3 markets). Costs: real FTMO spreads and swaps; 1.5x cost; halves 2010-17 / 2018 on (gold from 2008-06). Data in marketdata/fred/ (also marketdata/volidx, vixidx); research only to 2025-10-10. Expected net Sharpe 0.2-0.5 alone, low corr with the intraday book (weeks hold). Risk: equity VRP predictability weaker after 2005; US500 is only 4% of book risk. Suits Funded; Hydra no. No earlier test of an IV-RV gap in the repo (memory search found only dropped sources that said 'needs implied vols'; the series are now on disk).
result: Gate halves FAIL (-0.03 / 0.39); also belief 2/3 markets, corr hold +0.32, book 3.34->3.29. Only US500 works (SR 0.61); gold h1 -0.25, EURUSD -0.36. research/vrp_gap.py

title: G10 FX carry, monthly, net of broker swap markup: Lustig-Roussanov-Verdelhan (2011) and Menkhoff-Sarno-Schmeling-Schrimpf (2012) with the volatility cut
why: Gap: carry style (none in book), days-to-weeks horizon. Rule (from steer.md): on the first trading day each month rank USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, AUD, CHF, NZD by 3-month rate (IR3TIB01 files in marketdata/fred; previous month's value, past-only). Long the 2 highest, short the 2 lowest, each vs USD through FTMO pairs (EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD, USDCHF; crosses AUDJPY/GBPJPY where listed), equal risk, hold one month. Variant B (Menkhoff et al.): flat when 22-day realized FX vol (average of the pairs) is above its trailing-year 80th percentile. Cost: P&L = spot move + (rate gap - broker markup); markup estimated as today's rate gap minus today's FTMO swap (docs/ftmo_specs.json: AUDJPY long +4.27 / short -15.34 points per lot per night; GBPJPY long +5.14 / short -25.36) and subtracted from the rate gap in every past month; spread at 1.5x too. Halves 2002-17 / 2018 on (JP rates from 2002-04). Known risk: Hsu et al. find carry weak OOS and the markup eats most of the gap, so aim is net Sharpe 0.2-0.4 with corr <= 0.30 to the book (check losing months 2021-11, 2023-05 for overlap with yen-cross legs). Differs from earlier dropped carry notes, which stopped at 'needs rate series': the series and the markup recipe now exist. Suits Funded; Hydra no.
result: Gate halves FAIL (-0.11 / -0.16), 1.5x -0.23, belief 3/7 pairs; vol-cut variant SR 0.14. Spot data from 2009. research/fx_carry_g10.py

title: Policy-rate differential change as EURUSD (and GBPUSD, USDJPY) trend signal, weeks horizon (rate-gap predictors of FX; Engel-West / uncovered-interest-parity momentum)
why: Gap: EURUSD (no leg), weeks horizon, fundamental (not price) signal. Rule (steer.md): daily policy rates ECBDFR, DFF, IUDSOIA (marketdata/fred), JP from IR3TIB01JPM156N. For each pair: gap = foreign minus USD rate; signal = sign of the 63-business-day change in gap (past-only, rates lagged 1 day). Long EUR vs USD when the EUR-USD gap has risen over 3 months, short when fallen; same rule on GBPUSD (IUDSOIA minus DFF) and USDJPY (JP minus US). Rebalance weekly (Monday), hold 1 week, vol-scaled to equal risk; a 126-day variant as a second fixed setting, no sweep. Belief: 3 pairs, same parameters, economic reason (rate expectations drive flows); builder to read a source paper in full first (the link is the Menkhoff-family NBER paper on rate-driven FX returns, weak match to this exact rule). Costs: FTMO swaps and 1.5x spread; halves 2000-17 / 2018 on (ECB from 1999). Expected net Sharpe 0.2-0.4, corr to intraday book near 0; check overlap with the hold (trend, weeks+) leg and USDJPY exposure (25% of risk). Suits Funded; Hydra no.
result: gates FAIL at halves: SR -0.15, halves 0.12/-0.44, 1.5x -0.22, 1/3 pairs (research/policy_gap.py)

title: BSIC: buy the S&P when VIX/VIX3M spikes above its Bollinger band (long-only fear-spike dip buy), applied to US500, US100, GRXEUR
why: Gap: volatility-premium style via a term-structure signal (marketdata/vixidx/^VIX.csv and ^VIX3M.csv are on disk), US indices (4% of risk), days horizon, and the book losing months (a crash-buy pays after the stress that hurts trend/breakout legs; expect corr near 0). Rule as published (page read in full): ratio = VIX/VIX3M (VXV); z = (ratio - 20d mean) / 20d std; enter long at the next open (lag 1, past-only) when z > 1.5; exit when z falls back below 1.5 (back inside the bands); long only. Published: daily closes 2006-07 to 2015-11, post-cost Sharpe about 1 per trade return vs 0.34 for buy-and-hold, cost 0.05% per transaction; other parameter sets showed Sharpe 4-5 but with too few trades, so use only 20d / 1.5, no sweep. Our test: signal from VIX/VIX3M closes (VIX3M starts 2007), trade US500.cash, US100.cash, and GRXEUR proxy (same parameters; belief by 2-3 markets; XAUUSD as a control only), FTMO spread plus long swap from docs/ftmo_specs.json, halves 2007-17 / 2018 on (VIX3M history is short, report trade count per half), 1.5x cost, corr to book and book gain. Expected weakness: few trades (about 5-8 a year), long-equity beta (vrp_gap worked only on US500 for that reason: check corr to hold >0.30 and beta-only explanation by comparing with a random same-length long). Differs from rejected vrp_gap (IV minus RV level, weekly hold) and opex/totm (calendar). Suits Funded; Hydra no.
result: gates FAIL halves 0.66/-0.25, belief 2/3 markets, book 3.34->3.19; beta-like (random-long control SR 0.24/0.40/0.09 vs rule 0.27/0.31/-0.10); data starts 2010. research/vix_vxv_spike.py

title: Currency value (real exchange rate) cross-section on G10 via FTMO pairs: Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling, Schrimpf (2017), Currency Value, RFS 30(2)
why: Gap: a style not in the book (value, distinct from the rejected carry and policy-gap tests), EURUSD and the dollar pairs from a fundamental long-horizon signal, weeks+ horizon, expected corr near 0 (signal moves over years, traded quarterly). Paper read pp1-24 of 54 (definitions, portfolio construction, Tables 4 intro). Definitions: log real rate q = p_US - p_foreign - s (s = USD per unit of foreign currency; higher q = foreign currency cheap). Value signal x_j = 5-year change of q, d5q = q_t - q_(t-5y). Linear weights w_j = c*(x_j - mean_x), c scales sum|w| = 1, rebalanced end of each quarter; rank-weight and quartile-sort versions give the same picture. Paper result 1970-2014, 22 currencies, no costs: Sharpe 0.44-0.51 for the three constructions (macro-adjusted version 0.8-0.9 needs GDP, NFA, export-quality data we lack: do not build it). Our test: USD-based pairs EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD, USDCHF (7 currencies; EUR pre-1999 use DEM via FRED DEXGEUS if wanted, else start 2004). Spot from FRED daily DEXUSEU, DEXUSUK, DEXUSAL, DEXUSNZ, DEXJPUS, DEXCAUS, DEXSZUS (data item data_fred_fx_cpi), CPI from FRED monthly CPIAUCSL and OECD CPI series for each country (CPALTT01xxM661N or the quarterly ones), published with a lag so use CPI lagged 2 months. Position: each quarter-end the linear weights x_j - mean, long cheap/short rich vs USD, vol-scaled to equal risk per leg, held a quarter, executed on FTMO pairs with real spread and swap (carry paid by the position is part of the real P&L: use the FTMO swap in docs/ftmo_specs.json, plus rate-gap proxy from IR3TIB01 files in marketdata/fred for pre-2018 years, 1.5x costs). Halves: trades from 2009 (spot) to 2017 / 2018 on, signal needs 5y of history before. Belief: 7 currencies same parameters, published rule. Only 2 params (5y window, quarterly rebalance), no sweep. Expected net Sharpe 0.2-0.4 on 7 currencies and only 16 years of quarterly decisions (64 rebalances): few, so DSR/halves may fail; state that honestly. Differs from rejected fx_carry_g10 (rate sort) and policy_gap (3-month rate change): value is a price-level/inflation signal, known to be nearly independent of carry (paper Sec 4.3, Table 9). Suits Funded; Hydra no.
